title: NorthBridge Bank — PoC weekly check-in (week 2)
next_steps: Redwood to send updated benchmark summary (p50/p95 latency + throughput) with test config details (batching, context lengths) by Fri 2025-05-30.
NorthBridge Security to confirm required audit log fields and preferred export mechanism (S3 vs HTTPS push) and whether 7-day temporary retention is acceptable for PoC by Mon 2025-06-02.
Redwood to share evidence pack index + initiate SOC 2 report request workflow under NDA (Olga/Naomi) by Fri 2025-05-30.
Schedule a 30-min security follow-up focused on audit log export + KMS boundaries (Tom + Evan) for Tue/Wed next week.
Avery to set intro with NorthBridge vendor risk/procurement for early commercial/process check (order form, DPA, SLA) week of 2025-06-03.
Tentatively hold PoC closeout meeting week of 2025-06-10 to review success criteria and rollout path.
action_items: Owner: Evan Scott — Provide sample audit log payload + field mapping (actor, request_id, model_id, policy decision, timestamps) and note which fields are available today vs roadmap. Due: 2025-05-30
Owner: Olga Petrov — Send SOC 2 request instructions + list of standard security artifacts available in evidence pack; confirm NDA needed for report. Due: 2025-05-30
Owner: Avery Johnson — Draft procurement preview email (Dedicated vs Private options, contracting path, estimated timelines) and coordinate intro with Marta. Due: 2025-05-29
Owner: Nina Patel — Share updated traffic replay assumptions for week 3 (target QPS, context length distribution, streaming on/off) and confirm weekend load window. Due: 2025-05-31
Owner: Tom Gallagher — Clarify bank requirement for log immutability / WORM storage and whether exporting to existing SIEM satisfies audit expectations. Due: 2025-06-02
questions: Can Redwood guarantee that prompts/responses are not stored beyond configured retention in a VPC deployment (and what’s the default behavior in the PoC environment)?
What audit log schema is available today, and can we get deterministic fields for policy decisions, user identity, and export status?
How does customer-managed KMS work for envelope keys at rest, and does Redwood ever see plaintext keys?
If we move from VPC to on-prem later, does the control plane/telemetry model change materially?
What’s the expected procurement path (DPA, SLA, vendor risk) and can we start that before the PoC is fully complete?
summary: Week 2 PoC check-in with NorthBridge covering benchmark progress against success criteria (latency/throughput, error rate), security team feedback (audit logs, retention, KMS, SOC 2 evidence), and early procurement signals. Platform team reports improved p95 latency after tuning continuous batching and stream settings; remaining gap is audit log export format + retention controls clarity. Vendor risk asks for early visibility into contracting path and whether Redwood can transact via AWS Marketplace/private offer. Agreed on a security follow-up next week and an early procurement intro while technical validation continues.
topics: Benchmark results vs PoC success criteria (p95 latency, throughput, tail stability)
Integration status (routing, streaming, retries, SDK vs REST)
Security feedback: audit logs, SSO/SAML identity mapping, retention/residency, KMS/HSM boundaries
Evidence pack + SOC 2 report request process
Early procurement/process check: DPA/SLA, commercial path, Marketplace option
Next meetings and PoC closeout timeline
transcript:
Meeting: NorthBridge Bank — PoC weekly check-in (week 2)
Recorded: 2025-05-28 14:05 ET
Duration: 46 min
Attendees (Redwood): Avery Johnson (AE), Evan Scott (SE), Olga Petrov (GRC)
Attendees (NorthBridge): Nina Patel (Platform Eng), Tom Gallagher (Security Eng), Marta Ruiz (Vendor Risk)

[00:00] Avery Johnson: Hey everyone, good to see you. Um, I know we have Nina, Tom, and Marta on. Thanks for jumping on. Plan is quick: week two results versus the success criteria, what’s blocking security sign-off, and then—Marta—any early procurement process items so we’re not waiting till the very end.

[00:18] Nina Patel: Sounds good.

[00:20] Tom Gallagher: Yep.

[00:22] Marta Ruiz: Works.

[00:26] Evan Scott: I can share screen when we get to metrics. I’ve got the updated run from last night.

[00:34] Avery Johnson: Great. Nina, you want to kick with where you are integration-wise?

[00:40] Nina Patel: Sure. So we’re basically doing the same replay harness as week one, but we changed two things: we turned on streaming in the client for the “agent assist” style requests, and we adjusted the concurrency up. We also adjusted the batch settings based on your recs—continuous batching, I think you called it “cont batch”—and that helped.

[00:58] Nina Patel: We’re seeing fewer long tail spikes. The p95 got better. Not perfect, but like better than week one. The app team stopped complaining as much.

[01:09] Evan Scott: Nice.

[01:10] Avery Johnson: Can you remind everyone the success criteria you wrote down? Just so we’re all aligned.

[01:16] Nina Patel: Yep. For this PoC we said: p95 under 900 milliseconds for the typical 300 to 600 token outputs, with input context around 2k tokens, at—what did we say—20 requests per second equivalent during bursts. And error rate under 0.5%. And then the security side is like, no prompt retention, exportable audit logs, and KMS. Those were the big buckets.

[01:41] Tom Gallagher: And identity. We want to know who did what. That’s the other big bucket.

[01:46] Avery Johnson: Right, identity/auditability.

[01:49] Evan Scott: Okay. Let me share my screen. One sec.

[02:02] Evan Scott: You should see a spreadsheet-y thing. This is the run from 05/27 overnight. We’re using your harness config “nbb_replay_v2” and Redwood runtime config “rdw_profile_dedicated_vpc_02”—don’t read into the name, it’s basically the VPC profile.

[02:20] Evan Scott: For the median, p50 is around 420 milliseconds end-to-first-token, and p95 is around 860 on the streaming path. Non-streaming completion time is longer obviously, but for the user-perceived, it’s within the target.

[02:36] Nina Patel: That’s consistent with what we saw.

[02:38] Evan Scott: Tail-wise, p99 is still ~1.4 seconds. That’s the one I want to keep improving. We saw it correlate with context length outliers, like 6k+ input tokens.

[02:53] Nina Patel: Yeah we had a few long context things. Those are like the compliance policy docs. Not the typical chat.

[02:59] Avery Johnson: So for success criteria, you’re good on p95 for the typical distribution, but the long-context tail is still a bit high.

[03:06] Nina Patel: That’s fair.

[03:08] Evan Scott: Throughput-wise, we hit the 20 RPS burst for 10 minutes without dropping requests. There were a couple 429-ish looking things but those were on the client side, like your own retry budget.

[03:20] Nina Patel: Yeah that was our gateway.

[03:22] Evan Scott: Error rate is 0.2% on the Redwood side. Mostly timeouts when your harness killed the connection mid stream. So overall stable.

[03:35] Avery Johnson: Great. Tom, do you want to jump in on what you’re hearing from your side? You had some feedback last week around audit logs and retention.

[03:44] Tom Gallagher: Yep. So performance looks better, thanks. The issue is less performance, more: can we attest to controls. Like, we need audit logs that our audit team can accept. Right now what we saw in the sample log is missing a couple fields.

[03:59] Tom Gallagher: Specifically, we need a stable “actor” concept. Today it looks like service account name plus maybe an API key id, but we want it tied to SSO group or at least to a SAML assertion attribute. Also need a request ID that we can correlate end-to-end. You have request_id but it wasn’t in all events.

[04:21] Evan Scott: Yeah, that’s fair. Some events are “system” events vs request events. We can normalize that.

[04:26] Tom Gallagher: And then export. We need to get logs out. Prefer S3 bucket in our account or push to HTTPS endpoint, but it has to be near real-time, or at least every 5 minutes. The PoC currently is, like, we have to go in console and download.

[04:44] Avery Johnson: Got it. So the gaps are export automation and field completeness.

[04:49] Tom Gallagher: Exactly. And retention. We heard “configurable retention,” but we need to be very careful with claims. Our requirement is essentially no storage of prompts/responses, or a very short TTL that we can set. If there’s any logging that includes payloads, that’s a no-go. Like I don’t want prompts in logs.

[05:09] Evan Scott: Totally. We do not log prompt bodies in the audit trail. There are optional debug logs in some components, but we can disable that in private/VPC deployments. For the PoC environment, we can confirm what’s on.

[05:23] Olga Petrov: Just to add, on the compliance side, we have standard language around “customer config” and what’s logged. We should send you the formal doc rather than us ad-libbing.

[05:35] Tom Gallagher: Please. Because my team writes down what’s said and then vendor risk will hold you to it.

[05:40] Avery Johnson: Yep, understood. We’ll keep it tight.

[05:44] Marta Ruiz: And from my side, that’s exactly what we need. I’m not here to slow this down, but we need the evidence artifacts early. If we wait until week 6, it just pushes out.

[05:54] Avery Johnson: Makes sense.

[05:55] Marta Ruiz: So two questions: one, do you have SOC 2 Type II and can we get it under NDA? Two, what’s your contracting path: do you do DPAs, SLAs, and do you transact via AWS Marketplace? We have a faster track if it’s marketplace. Not required, but faster.

[06:15] Avery Johnson: Yes to SOC 2 under NDA; Olga can speak to the process. On Marketplace, we can do private offers in some cases—depends on structure. We should do an intro with you and our legal/commercial folks to align.

[06:30] Olga Petrov: For SOC 2, we do have Type II. We can share the report under NDA through our secure portal. Usually it’s a standard request—Marta, we’ll send the instructions, you sign the NDA if you haven’t already, and then we grant time-limited access.

[06:47] Marta Ruiz: Okay.

[06:49] Tom Gallagher: Also, do you have ISO?

[06:52] Olga Petrov: We have an ISO-aligned program; I’ll confirm what certificates are current for sharing. SOC 2 is the main artifact we share in these reviews.

[07:03] Tom Gallagher: Fine. And for incident response, we’ll ask later.

[07:07] Avery Johnson: Evan, can we talk audit logs details? Tom’s point about fields and export.

[07:13] Evan Scott: Yeah. So, today in Private deployments we support audit log export via a few patterns. The cleanest for your world is: logs written as JSON lines to an internal bucket and then forwarded to your destination. In VPC, we can configure it to write to S3 in your account, assuming the role, or to push to an HTTPS collector.

[07:35] Evan Scott: For the PoC, we didn’t turn on automated export because we wanted to validate schema first. That might have been a mistake; we can enable it this week.

[07:45] Tom Gallagher: Good.

[07:46] Evan Scott: On fields, we have: timestamp, request_id, org_id, project_id, model_id, route name, result status, tokens in/out, and actor. The actor is usually the API key + optionally a user id if you’re using SSO via the Console. For service-to-service, we need to map your gateway identity into a header and then include that in audit. We can do that.

[08:13] Nina Patel: We can pass a user id from our app, yes.

[08:16] Tom Gallagher: But it must be non-spoofable. Like if it’s a header, we need to sign it or ensure it’s from our gateway.

[08:22] Evan Scott: Understood. In VPC we can set network policies so only your gateway can reach the endpoint. Also we can require mutual TLS on that hop if needed. But for PoC, we can just validate the shape.

[08:35] Avery Johnson: Tom, does that satisfy the requirement directionally?

[08:38] Tom Gallagher: Directionally. I need to see a sample payload with the fields and an explanation of where each value comes from.

[08:46] Evan Scott: I can send a sample payload and a field mapping doc by Friday.

[08:51] Tom Gallagher: Great.

[08:54] Avery Johnson: Retention: you said “no prompt retention,” can you clarify what you need to hear?

[09:01] Tom Gallagher: I need to hear “we can configure it so prompts/responses are not stored,” and if there are exceptions, you enumerate them. Like, caches. KV cache. Whatever. If you keep stuff in memory for performance, that’s fine. If you write to disk, we need to know.

[09:18] Evan Scott: Okay. So, caches are in-memory on the serving runtime. We don’t persist prompts to disk as part of normal serving. There are operational logs and metrics, but those don’t include full payloads. For troubleshooting, there’s an optional request/response logging feature—off by default in regulated configs.

[09:38] Tom Gallagher: “Off by default” is good, but we’ll want it contractually represented.

[09:42] Avery Johnson: Noted.

[09:44] Olga Petrov: We have language in our security FAQ about data handling and retention. I’ll send that and we can do a follow-up security session so we don’t do it in piecemeal.

[09:55] Nina Patel: Also, we had that SSO thing. Not sure if Tom wants to bring it up.

[09:59] Tom Gallagher: Yeah. We tried to hook SAML to your console for the admin roles. It kind of worked, then failed with metadata validation. We opened a ticket—someone said it’s because of a signature algo mismatch? Not sure.

[10:13] Evan Scott: I saw that. Our support team said it was an IdP metadata parsing edge case. We have a workaround: remove the unused certificate block and re-upload. We can hop on with your identity person. That’s not really blocking PoC, but it matters for production.

[10:31] Tom Gallagher: It matters. If we can’t do SSO, we can’t proceed.

[10:35] Avery Johnson: Totally. Let’s treat it as a priority fix.

[10:38] Olga Petrov: And SCIM provisioning—do you need that as well?

[10:41] Tom Gallagher: Eventually, yes. For now SAML SSO is the must.

[10:46] Avery Johnson: Okay.

[10:48] Marta Ruiz: Just to tie this together: vendor risk is going to ask for your security doc set, and also the “shared responsibility model” for VPC. Like what’s on you vs on us.

[11:00] Evan Scott: Yeah, we can provide that. In Private/VPC, you own the network perimeter, and we provide the control plane and runtime updates; logs can be sent to your SIEM; keys through your KMS integration. We’ll document.

[11:14] Avery Johnson: Marta, if we start the procurement conversation early, what’s the gating path? Like what can we do while PoC continues.

[11:22] Marta Ruiz: We can start vendor onboarding. The biggest long pole is legal review of the DPA and any SLA. Also our infosec will want the SOC 2 and likely a questionnaire. If you can answer quickly, it helps.

[11:38] Avery Johnson: Great. We’re set up to respond quickly—we have an evidence pack and standard answers, and Olga’s team can help.

[11:45] Tom Gallagher: I’m going to ask you a questionnaire, sorry.

[11:47] Avery Johnson: Totally expected.

[11:50] Nina Patel: Can we talk about Dedicated vs Private? Because our platform team thinks VPC Private is likely, but finance is going to ask if Dedicated hosted is enough.

[11:59] Avery Johnson: Yep. The quick version: Dedicated is reserved capacity in Redwood’s environment with isolation at the compute level, but not in your VPC. Private is in your VPC or on-prem with tighter network controls and often better fit for regulated. We can walk through the trade-offs.

[12:15] Marta Ruiz: For us, anything not in our VPC is harder. Not impossible, just slower.

[12:19] Tom Gallagher: Yeah, VPC is preferred. Our policy is “customer data stays in customer boundary.”

[12:25] Evan Scott: That matches the current deployment you’re testing.

[12:28] Nina Patel: Performance wise, are we giving up anything by doing VPC?

[12:32] Evan Scott: Not necessarily. It depends on your hardware profile. The main differences are operational: upgrades, monitoring, and how we route. But the runtime is basically the same.

[12:45] Avery Johnson: Okay. Evan, anything else on performance improvements for week three?

[12:50] Evan Scott: Two ideas: one, we can pin a more aggressive kernel profile for your common context lengths. Two, we can enable prefix caching for the policy doc prompts if you have repeated system prompts. That would help tail latency.

[13:05] Nina Patel: We do. The system prompt is repeated.

[13:07] Evan Scott: Great. We can test that.

[13:10] Tom Gallagher: Does caching mean you store stuff?

[13:12] Evan Scott: It’s an in-memory KV cache on the runtime. It’s not persisted. But we’ll document and you can decide.

[13:21] Tom Gallagher: Okay, as long as it’s memory only and within our VPC boundary.

[13:26] Avery Johnson: Cool.

[13:28] (crosstalk)

[13:29] Nina Patel: One more thing—our app team asked about regional isolation. We need US-only.

[13:35] Avery Johnson: For VPC deployment, you choose the region where it runs, so yes it stays in-region.

[13:41] Tom Gallagher: And support personnel access?

[13:44] Olga Petrov: We do least-privilege access controls. For Private deployments, access is gated and audited. We can share our access policy summary and the audit log approach.

[13:56] Tom Gallagher: Good.

[14:00] Avery Johnson: Let’s get tactical: what do we need to deliver between now and next check-in to avoid stalling.

[14:06] Tom Gallagher: Sample audit log payload, field mapping, and confirmation of no payload logging. Also fix SAML.

[14:14] Nina Patel: And for us, we’ll share the week three load window and new traffic profile.

[14:20] Marta Ruiz: For me, evidence pack index and a call with your contracting person, or at least a one-pager on process. Marketplace would be ideal.

[14:30] Avery Johnson: Okay.

[14:32] Evan Scott: On SAML, I can coordinate with our support team and schedule a 30 min with your identity engineer. Tom, do you have someone specific?

[14:40] Tom Gallagher: Yeah, I can pull in Jason from IAM.

[14:43] Evan Scott: Great.

[14:45] Avery Johnson: Olga, can you send evidence pack index and SOC2 process by Friday?

[14:50] Olga Petrov: Yes. I’ll send a short email with the index, what’s shareable without NDA, and how to request the SOC 2.

[14:58] Avery Johnson: Perfect.

[15:00] Avery Johnson: Marta, can you do early procurement intro next week? Like 25 minutes, just align on DPA and timeline.

[15:07] Marta Ruiz: Yes. Tuesday afternoon or Thursday morning works.

[15:12] Avery Johnson: I’ll propose times.

[15:15] Nina Patel: For the next technical check-in, we usually do Wednesdays. Same time next week?

[15:20] Avery Johnson: Works for me. Evan?

[15:22] Evan Scott: Yep.

[15:23] Tom Gallagher: I might not make that one. But I can do a security-focused follow-up separately.

[15:28] Avery Johnson: Great point. Let’s do two meetings: (1) regular PoC check-in Wed, (2) security follow-up Tue or Thu focusing audit logs + KMS + SSO. Evan and Olga can join.

[15:42] Tom Gallagher: That’s good.

[15:44] Evan Scott: On KMS: do you need HSM specifically?

[15:48] Tom Gallagher: Ideally integration with our KMS. HSM sometimes. For now, show that encryption keys are customer-managed.

[15:56] Evan Scott: Understood.

[16:00] Avery Johnson: Any concerns about the performance economics side? I know one of your drivers is cost predictability.

[16:07] Nina Patel: Not yet. We haven’t gotten far enough. We need a pricing model though. It’s hard to evaluate without at least ballpark.

[16:15] Avery Johnson: We can share a range once we pick Dedicated vs Private shape. For PoC we usually keep it simple, but given procurement is in the loop, I can give a preliminary estimate and then refine.

[16:26] Marta Ruiz: Please keep it in writing, not just verbal.

[16:29] Avery Johnson: Yep.

[16:31] Tom Gallagher: And no “HIPAA ready” language please. Our lawyers hate that. (laughs)

[16:36] Avery Johnson: Understood. We’ll stick to concrete controls.

[16:39] Evan Scott: (laughs) Noted.

[16:41] Avery Johnson: Okay, I’ll recap.

[16:44] Avery Johnson: Performance: p95 is within target for typical distribution; we’re still improving p99 for long context. Next week we’ll test prefix caching and a tuned kernel profile. Security: top gaps are audit log field mapping + export automation, and SAML metadata issue. Olga will send evidence pack index + SOC2 process; Evan will send sample audit log payload and schedule SAML troubleshooting with Jason.

[17:09] Avery Johnson: Procurement: Marta and I will set a 25 minute intro next week to align on DPA/SLA path and marketplace option.

[17:17] Avery Johnson: Meetings: Wed same time for week three check-in; and separate security follow-up Tue or Thu.

[17:25] Nina Patel: Sounds good.

[17:27] Tom Gallagher: Works.

[17:28] Marta Ruiz: Yes.

[17:30] Avery Johnson: Cool. Anything else before we drop?

[17:33] Nina Patel: Nope.

[17:34] Tom Gallagher: All good.

[17:36] Marta Ruiz: Thanks.

[17:38] Avery Johnson: Thanks everyone.

(End of transcript excerpt — Fireflies continued with scheduling chatter and calendar invites for ~2 minutes.)
